provider: DVC remotes (S3 / WebDAV / SSH / HTTP / Drive) pointed at free backends

free_tier.stated: N/A — DVC ships no storage; the remote is whatever free store you configure. Free-tier bytes = the backing store's bytes. Supports Amazon S3 + S3-compatible (MinIO etc. via `endpointurl`), Azure Blob, GCS, Google Drive, Aliyun OSS, SSH/SFTP, HDFS/WebHDFS, HTTP, WebDAV.

egress.terms: Inherited. The HTTP remote is read-only and can sit behind any CDN, which is the only path where DVC itself doesn't add egress cost.

tooling: `dvc` CLI + dvcfilesystem (fsspec). `dvc remote add s3://bucket && dvc remote modify myremote endpointurl https://s3.hf.co/<ns>` works. Native read-only Git-LFS support means `dvc get`/`dvc import` can pull straight from a Hugging Face repo without installing git-lfs.
chaining: One repo, many remotes (`dvc remote add` x N), plus `dvc push -r <remote>` to pick. Any S3-compatible free endpoint multiplies: HF buckets, IA's IAS3, MinIO on a free VM, an Oracle/Cloudflare-adjacent free tier. DVC's content-addressed cache means the same 20 TiB corpus can be pushed to N stores and only the missing blobs transfer.
limits_note: No per-file logic of its own; the backend's limits apply. WebDAV is the weakest link (DVC's WebDAV support is newer and less battle-tested than S3). HTTP remote is read-only, so it cannot be a primary. No built-in retry-sharding across remotes — you script it.
reliability_note: DVC is an ML-tooling project (treeverse); remote support quality varies by backend. S3-compatible endpoints need `endpointurl` + often `use_ssl`/path-style tweaks. Reliability is effectively the backend's.
